data.title: Ship
data.label: Part 1
data.lede: In this part, you will scaffold a blog, deploy it on Cloudflare, sign up as the admin, and change the content model.

concepts.title: An [Astro integration](https://docs.emdashcms.com/concepts/architecture/)
concepts.text: EmDash can be thought of as an Astro integration. Admin, [REST API](https://docs.emdashcms.com/reference/rest-api/), auth, media and plugins come with `emdash()` in your [Astro config](https://docs.emdashcms.com/reference/configuration/).

concepts.title: Cloudflare primitives
concepts.text: Your EmDash site runs on [Cloudflare Workers](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/), [D1](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/) holds content, [R2](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/) stores media. Your site can also run on [Node with SQLite or Postgres](https://docs.emdashcms.com/deployment/nodejs/).

concepts.title: Content lives in the database
concepts.text: Each [collection](https://docs.emdashcms.com/concepts/collections/) is a real SQL table (`ec_posts`). Rich text is [Portable Text](https://portabletext.org/), which is structured JSON, not HTML.

data.title: Automate
data.label: Part 2
data.lede: Your EmDash site already comes with an [MCP server](https://docs.emdashcms.com/reference/mcp-server/). In this part, you will connect your agent to it and let it handle the content for your site.

concepts.title: [MCP server](https://docs.emdashcms.com/reference/mcp-server/)
concepts.text: Built into every site at `/_emdash/api/mcp`. Agents use it to work with content.

concepts.title: [CLI](https://docs.emdashcms.com/reference/cli/)
concepts.text: `npx emdash content …` and `schema …`. Outputs JSON, good for scripts and CI.

concepts.title: [Agent skills](https://docs.emdashcms.com/agent-skills/)
concepts.text: In `.agents/skills/`. They teach coding agents the current EmDash APIs, so they don't make mistakes.

concepts.title: Least privilege
concepts.text: [OAuth scopes](https://docs.emdashcms.com/reference/mcp-server/#authentication) and [user roles](https://docs.emdashcms.com/guides/authentication/#user-roles) are checked separately. Scopes let you restrict the token to only the permissions it needs.

data.title: Extend
data.label: Part 3
data.lede: You deployed your EmDash blog, and configured an agent to manage the content. You also asked the agent to make code changes. In this part, you will build a plugin that generates a cover image for your posts. You will also learn about the security aspect of the plugin.

concepts.title: The problem
concepts.text: On WordPress, [most security vulnerabilities come from plugins](https://patchstack.com/whitepaper/state-of-wordpress-security-in-2025/). Any plugin can read every key stored in the site and send it anywhere.

concepts.title: [A manifest is a contract](https://docs.emdashcms.com/plugins/creating-plugins/manifest/)
concepts.text: `emdash-plugin.jsonc` lists the [capabilities](https://docs.emdashcms.com/plugins/creating-plugins/capabilities/) and hosts a plugin needs. Nothing else is available to it.

concepts.title: Same plugin, two ways to run
concepts.text: `sandboxed: []` gives it [its own isolate](https://docs.emdashcms.com/deployment/plugin-sandbox/). `plugins: []` runs it in-process, with the same API gates but no isolation.

data.title: Check your setup
data.label: Check your setup
data.lede: Paste this into your coding agent to check your machine and resolve missing dependencies. It will ask before installing or updating anything and will tell you to log in to Cloudflare yourself if you aren't already.

items.label: Dependencies
items.text: [Node 22.16+](https://nodejs.org/), [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/installation), [git](https://git-scm.com/), [Wrangler](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/), and a Cloudflare account with [R2](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/) enabled

body.label: Agent-assisted setup
body.text:
Check that my machine is ready for the EmDash CMS workshop.

1. Check: `node -v` (v22.16 or newer), `pnpm -v`, `git --version`, `npx wrangler@latest whoami`.
2. Missing or outdated tool: tell me the install command for my OS and ask before you run it. For pnpm, prefer `corepack enable pnpm`.
3. Not signed in to Cloudflare: don't sign in for me. Tell me to run `npx wrangler login` myself (it opens my browser), wait for me, then check again.
4. More than one Cloudflare account: list them in the table and ask me which one I'll use for the workshop. Don't save it anywhere: we'll set it when we deploy.
5. Check that R2 is enabled on that account: `npx wrangler r2 bucket list`. With more than one account, run it as `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=<id> npx wrangler r2 bucket list`, or Wrangler refuses to pick one. If it says R2 isn't enabled (error 10042), tell me to open the Cloudflare dashboard, go to R2, and enable it (it may ask for a payment method, even on the free plan). Wait for me, then check again.
6. Tell me which coding agent you are, and confirm you can connect to remote MCP servers over HTTP with OAuth.

Ignore Wrangler warnings about missing optional permissions: the workshop doesn't need them.

Finish with a short table (tool, status, version or account), then "Ready" or what's left to fix. Don't create or deploy anything yet.

data.title: Create your blog
data.label: Create your blog
data.lede: With a single command you can scaffold an [Astro site](https://astro.build/) with EmDash, [the Blog template](https://github.com/emdash-cms/templates/tree/main/blog-cloudflare), and [agent skills](https://docs.emdashcms.com/agent-skills/). These agent skills teach your agent current EmDash APIs.

items.label: Template
items.text: Blog on Cloudflare Workers, with sample posts.

body.label: Copy this prompt into your agent
body.text:
Create a new EmDash blog for the EmDash CMS workshop. {{narrate}}

1. Make a workshop folder and go into it: `mkdir -p {{workspaceDir}} && cd {{workspaceDir}}`.
2. Scaffold the site without prompts: `pnpm create emdash@latest {{siteDir}} --template cloudflare:blog --pm pnpm --install --no-sandboxed-plugins`.
No need to explain Sandboxed plugins. We will look at it later in the workshop.
If the install fails and the project files are still created, show me the error, and we'll fix it and run `pnpm install` inside `{{siteDir}}`.
3. Inside `{{siteDir}}`: if it isn't a git repository yet, run `git init`. Then `git add -A && git commit -m "Scaffold EmDash blog"`, so every later change shows up as a diff.
4. In at most three short sentences, tell me what this project is: what EmDash adds to Astro, where content and media will live on Cloudflare, and that `.agents/skills/` and `AGENTS.md` hold instructions you'll use later. No file names beyond those.
5. Give me the folder's full path and the exact commands to restart you inside it, with one line on why.

Keep your whole reply short. Don't deploy yet.

children.text: You should see a short summary of the project and its full path.

data.title: Deploy to Cloudflare
data.label: Deploy to Cloudflare
data.lede:
The [first deploy](https://docs.emdashcms.com/deployment/cloudflare/) creates everything the site needs: a [D1 database](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/), an [R2 bucket](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/), a [KV namespace](https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/) for sessions, and [the Worker](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/). Later deploys reuse them.

The prompt below has your agent check that you're logged in to Cloudflare and, if you have more than one account, use the one you picked. It then deploys your site, which creates those resources, and stores the encryption key from your `.env` as a Worker secret.

body.label: Copy this prompt into your agent
body.text:
Deploy my EmDash blog to Cloudflare Workers. {{explain}}

Steps:

1. Run `pnpm wrangler whoami`. Only if it lists more than one account: ask me which one to use (the one I picked in the setup check), then add `"account_id": "<id>"` at the top level of `wrangler.jsonc`.
   Explain: deploys and secrets in this folder now use this account, in any terminal.
2. Deploy: `pnpm run deploy`. Ignore the warnings about `workers_dev` and `preview_urls`: the defaults are what we want.
   Explain: what this first deploy creates (a D1 database for content, an R2 bucket for media, a KV namespace for sessions, and the Worker), and that later deploys reuse them.
   If it fails with code 10014 ("a namespace with this … title already exists"), a KV namespace is left over from an earlier attempt: show me `pnpm wrangler kv namespace list`, and ask before deleting it.
3. Store the encryption key from `.env` as a Worker secret, without printing it: `grep '^EMDASH_ENCRYPTION_KEY=' .env | cut -d= -f2- | pnpm wrangler secret put EMDASH_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
   Explain: `.env` never leaves my machine, and in Part 3 the site needs this key to encrypt the plugin's API token.
4. If anything in the repo changed, commit it: `git add -A && git commit -m "Deploy to Cloudflare"`.
   Explain: in one line, what changed.

Then stop. Don't open the site or the admin: I'll open them myself, straight away. Tell me the first load can take up to half a minute while the site sets up its database. End your reply with two links on their own lines: my site, then my site with `/_emdash/admin` on the end.

body.label: Copy this prompt into your agent
body.text:
I added two fields to Posts in my live site's admin: `featured` (boolean) and `subtitle` (short text). Use them on the homepage. {{explain}}

Steps:

1. Sign the EmDash CLI in to my live site: `npx emdash login --url <my site URL>`. It shows a code and a link: give me both, tell me to open the link and approve, and wait for me.
   Explain: the content model lives in the live database, not in the repo, so the CLI needs access to read it.
2. Generate types from the live schema: `npx emdash types --url <my site URL>`. Show me only the lines for `featured` and `subtitle` in `.emdash/types.ts`.
   These are standalone types. The site's own types are in `emdash-env.d.ts`, which `pnpm dev` generates from the local database, and that doesn't have the new fields. So copy the two lines into the `Post` interface in `emdash-env.d.ts`.
   Explain: why the types come from a running site and not from a file in the repo.
3. Use the `building-emdash-site` skill. Under the site title, the homepage (`src/pages/index.astro`) shows a featured post card, drawn by `src/components/PostCard.astro` with `variant="feature"`. Change it so the card shows the newest post where `featured` is true, falling back to the newest post when none is, and leave that post out of the grid below. Query it with `getEmDashCollection("posts", { where: { featured: true }, orderBy: { published_at: "desc" }, limit: 1 })`. EmDash's `WhereValue` type doesn't list booleans yet, although the query works, so cast the value (`true as unknown as WhereValue`, with `WhereValue` imported from `emdash`) and add a one-line comment saying why. Show the post's `subtitle` under its title when it has one, in the `feature` variant only: the grid cards use the same component. Show me only the lines you changed.
   Explain: in one line, what `where` does here, and that `posts` is a real SQL table behind the scenes.
4. Run `pnpm run typecheck`, commit, then deploy with `pnpm run deploy`.
   Explain: local `pnpm dev` uses a separate local database that has neither the new fields nor my content, so we check the change on the deployed site.

End by telling me to open my site (URL on its own line) and check that the featured post card under the site title shows the post I marked as featured, with its subtitle.

Bring my site to the workshop's Checkpoint A. {{narrate}}

1. In a temporary folder, fetch the checkpoint: `npx giget@latest gh:{{repo}}#checkpoint-a /tmp/emdash-checkpoint-a`.

data.title: Connect your agent
data.label: Connect your agent
data.lede: In this step, you will add your site as an [MCP server](https://docs.emdashcms.com/reference/mcp-server/). When you sign in, your site [asks what the agent may do](https://docs.emdashcms.com/reference/mcp-server/#authentication). You select the scopes to provide only the required access to the agent.

children.text: The prompt below asks the agent to:
Identify which agent it is, because the steps to connect an MCP server differ between agents.
Connect itself to your site's MCP server.
Tell you which permissions to select.

body.label: Copy this prompt into your agent
body.text:
Connect yourself to my EmDash site's MCP server, so you can work with its content. {{narrate}}

The server URL is my live site's URL with `/_emdash/api/mcp` on the end. Name the server `emdash-site`.

1. Tell me which agent you are, then add the server:
   - Claude Code: run `claude mcp add --transport http emdash-site <URL>`, then tell me to run `/mcp`, pick `emdash-site`, and authenticate.
   - Codex: run `codex mcp add emdash-site --url <URL>`, then ask me and run `codex mcp login emdash-site`.
   - OpenCode: add it as a remote server in `opencode.json`, then ask me and run `opencode mcp auth emdash-site`.
   - Cursor: tell me to open Cursor Settings → MCP, add a server with this URL, and click Connect.
   - VS Code: add it to `.vscode/mcp.json` under `servers` with `"type": "http"`, then tell me to click Start above it and use Copilot Chat in Agent mode.
   - Any other agent: tell me how to add a remote MCP server with this URL.
2. Tell me that my browser will open my site's consent screen. Every permission on it starts ticked, and it shows descriptions, not scope names. I keep exactly these five and untick everything else:
   - "Read content (posts, pages, etc.)" (`content:read`)
   - "Create, edit, and delete content; manage menus and taxonomies" (`content:write`)
   - "View media files" (`media:read`)
   - "Upload and manage media files" (`media:write`)
   - "View collection schemas" (`schema:read`)
   Unticking includes "Create and modify collection schemas" (`schema:write`), "Use MCP tools from all enabled plugins" (`mcp:tools`) and "Full administrative access" (`admin`).
3. Wait for me. Then tell me whether I need to restart you (if unsure, say yes), and to paste the next prompt from the workshop page.

Don't call any of the site's tools yet.

body.label: Edit the topic, then copy
body.text:
Topic: what a CMS conference in Poland taught me about content teams.

Do some editorial work on my site with this topic. {{mcpOnly}} Before each tool call, tell me in one line what it does.

1. Read the Posts schema first, so you know the fields before you write anything.
2. Draft three posts on the topic: title, subtitle, excerpt, and a few short paragraphs of content each. Leave them as drafts. No images: we'll generate covers in Part 3.
3. Create tags that fit, and assign them to the three drafts.
4. Write alt text for the sample posts' cover images. Set it on each post's `featured_image` field with `content_update`, not only on the media library item: the post keeps its own copy of `alt`, and that copy is what the site renders. Leave the SEO image (`seo.image`) alone: it only overrides the image used when the post is shared, and the site already falls back to `featured_image`.
5. Schedule one of the drafts for tomorrow at 9:00 my time.

End with a short table: post title, status, tags. Then tell me to open my admin (URL on its own line) and look at Posts.

data.title: Getting started with the plugin
data.label: Open the plugin starter
data.lede: You will use a starter template to scaffold the plugin. You'll modify this template and write the parts that are relevant for the workshop.

children.text: The prompt below instructs the agent to download the starter template, install its dependencies, and set it up for the next steps.

body.label: Copy this prompt into your agent
body.text:
Set up the Cover Images plugin starter next to my site. {{narrate}}

1. Download the starter into the workshop folder, next to `{{siteDir}}`: `npx giget@latest gh:{{repo}}/{{pluginDir}}#checkpoint-b {{workspaceDir}}/{{pluginDir}}`.
2. Install its dependencies, as one command: `cd {{workspaceDir}}/{{pluginDir}} && pnpm install`.
3. Ask me for my Atmosphere handle or DID (for example a Bluesky handle). Set it as `publisher` in `{{workspaceDir}}/{{pluginDir}}/emdash-plugin.jsonc`. If I don't have one, use the workshop placeholder `{{placeholderDid}}`.
4. Walk me through the starter in at most five short bullets: what's already done for us, and what's left to write (the trust contract, `generateCover`, the editor and agent entry points, the publish rule). Open files only to answer this.
5. From now on, work from `{{siteDir}}` and refer to the plugin as `../{{pluginDir}}`. If your shell isn't in `{{siteDir}}`, run `cd {{workspaceDir}}/{{siteDir}}` first.

Don't change anything else yet.

body.text:
Fill in the trust contract in `../{{pluginDir}}/emdash-plugin.jsonc`. Use the `creating-plugins` skill, and check field names with the EmDash docs MCP server. {{explain}}

Steps:

1. Set `capabilities` to exactly `network:request`, `content:write`, `content:revisions:read`, `media:write`, `hooks.content-policy:register`.
   Explain: what each one adds to `ctx`, why we don't also list `content:read` or `media:read`, and why reading a post's pending draft needs `content:revisions:read` on top of `content:write`.
2. Set `allowedHosts` to exactly `api.replicate.com` and `*.replicate.delivery`.
   Explain: Replicate serves generated files from `replicate.delivery` and its subdomains, and these are the only hosts `ctx.http` will let the plugin reach.
3. Under `admin`: a `/settings` page labelled "Settings", a `settingsSchema` with `replicateToken` (type `secret`, label "Replicate API token"), and an editor action `generate-cover` labelled "Generate cover", with `placement: "toolbar"` and `collections: ["posts"]`, that calls the private route `covers/generate`. `placement` is required: validate fails without it.
   Explain: what `type: "secret"` does to the token when it's stored.
4. Run `pnpm run validate` in `../{{pluginDir}}`.
   Explain: what validate checks, in one line.

Show me only the final `capabilities`, `allowedHosts` and `admin` blocks. Don't write plugin code yet.

data.title: Generate a cover
data.label: Generate a cover
data.lede: In this step, you will add a function that reads the post, asks [FLUX.2 [klein] 4B](https://replicate.com/black-forest-labs/flux-2-klein-4b) for an image, stores it, and sets it as the post's cover image.

items.label: Model
items.text: [FLUX.2 [klein] 4B](https://replicate.com/black-forest-labs/flux-2-klein-4b) on [Replicate](https://replicate.com/), about $0.001 an image and under a second to make.

items.label: Network
items.text: Two calls: create the prediction, download the image.

children.text: The prompt instructs the agent to write a function that reads the post, checks whether it already has a cover image, and calls Replicate with the API key from the plugin's settings. Once the image is generated, the function uploads it to EmDash and sets it as the cover image.

body.label: Copy this prompt into your agent
body.text:
In `../{{pluginDir}}/src/plugin.ts`, write one function, `generateCover(ctx, postId)`, that every entry point will share. Use the `creating-plugins` skill, and check each `ctx` API with the EmDash docs MCP server. {{explain}}

Steps:

1. Read the post with `ctx.content.get("posts", postId)`. `get` returns the saved post, not a pending draft, so if the post has a `draftRevisionId`, read the draft with `ctx.content.getRevision("posts", postId, post.draftRevisionId)` and use the draft's `data` from here on. If that `featured_image` is set, return it without generating anything. The post's fields sit under `data`; `post.seo.image` is the SEO panel's share image, not the cover, so ignore it. Check for an `id`, not `src`: EmDash drops `src` when it saves a library image and works out the URL when the page renders. Otherwise build an image prompt from the title and excerpt: an editorial illustration, with no text in the image.
   Explain: why returning early makes the function safe to call twice, and why we read the draft: a cover we staged, or an editor removing one, only exists there until someone publishes.
2. Read the token with `ctx.settings.get("replicateToken")`. If it's missing, return an error that tells the editor to add it under the plugin's Settings.
3. Call Replicate with `ctx.http.fetch`, never the global `fetch`: POST `https://api.replicate.com/v1/models/black-forest-labs/flux-2-klein-4b/predictions` with headers `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `Prefer: wait=20` and `Cancel-After: 25s`, and body `{ "input": { "prompt": <prompt>, "aspect_ratio": "16:9", "output_format": "webp" } }`. If `status` isn't `succeeded`, return a clear error. Don't poll.
   Explain: how `Prefer: wait` and `Cancel-After` keep us under the sandbox's 30-second wall time, and why polling would burn the 10-subrequest budget.
4. Download `output[0]` straight away with `ctx.http.fetch`, and read the bytes with `arrayBuffer()`.
   Explain: Replicate deletes API outputs after an hour, so the site keeps its own copy.
5. Upload it: `ctx.media.upload("cover.webp", "image/webp", bytes)`, which returns `{ mediaId, url }`.
6. Set the cover with `ctx.content.update("posts", postId, { featured_image: { id: mediaId, src: url, alt } })`, writing `alt` from the post's title. Don't set `seo.image`.
   Explain: posts keep revisions, so this stages a draft. The live page doesn't change until someone publishes.

Return `{ ok: true, mediaId, url }` or `{ ok: false, error }`. Don't connect it to any route or hook yet. Run `pnpm run typecheck` in `../{{pluginDir}}`, then show me the function.

children.text: The prompt instructs the agent to give the plugin two entry points: a button in the post editor, and an MCP tool.

body.label: Copy this prompt into your agent
body.text:
Give `generateCover` two entry points in `../{{pluginDir}}/src/plugin.ts`, both backed by private routes. Use the `creating-plugins` skill (its API routes and MCP tools reference). {{explain}}

Steps:

1. Editors: implement the private route `covers/generate` behind the "Generate cover" editor action. Give it the permission `content:edit_any`. Read the post from `routeCtx.ui.entry`, call `generateCover`, and reply with a toast and a refresh, so the editor sees the new cover.
   Explain: why the route reads the entry from `routeCtx.ui.entry` and not from the request body, and why we use `content:edit_any`: a plugin route checks only the user's role, not who owns the post or whether it's a draft, so `content:edit_own` or `content:edit_own_drafts` would let Authors or Contributors change anyone's post.
2. Agents: in `../{{pluginDir}}`, add `zod` at the exact version EmDash uses, or the tool's schema types won't match: `pnpm add -E "zod@$(node -p "require('./node_modules/emdash/package.json').dependencies.zod")"`. Add an MCP tool under `mcp.tools` named `generateCover`, with input `z.object({ postId: z.string() })`, pointing at a second private route with the same permission that reads `routeCtx.input`. Description: "Generate an AI cover image for a post that has none. Use it when publishing fails because a post has no cover."
   Explain: why the description matters to an agent, and why the tool doesn't need `destructive: true` (`generateCover` never replaces an existing cover).
3. Run `pnpm run validate` and `pnpm run typecheck`.
   Explain: the tool will show up as `{{pluginSlug}}__generateCover`, and calling it needs the token scope `mcp:tools` (or the narrower `mcp:tools:{{pluginSlug}}`), which your connection doesn't have yet.

Show me only the routes and the `mcp` block.

data.title: Enforce the publish rule
data.label: Enforce the publish rule
data.lede: In this step, you enforce a publish rule: a post without a cover image can't be published. This rule runs on [every path that publishes a post](https://docs.emdashcms.com/reference/content-lifecycle/), whether that's a person, the scheduler or an agent.

children.text: In the prompt below, the agent is instructed to update the code to make sure a cover image is present before a post is published.

body.label: Copy this prompt into your agent
body.text:
Make a cover image required for publishing, in `../{{pluginDir}}/src/plugin.ts`, and test it. {{explain}}

Steps:

1. Add a `content:beforePublish` hook. For the `posts` collection, when `event.content.data.featured_image` is empty, return `{ cancel: true, reason: "Add a cover image (try Generate cover)." }`. `event.content` is the whole content item, so the fields sit under `data`, next to `id`, `status` and `seo`. Check only `featured_image`, not `seo.image`.
   Explain: this hook runs on every way to publish: the admin, the REST API, MCP, the scheduler, and other plugins.
2. Register the same check as `content:beforeSchedule`.
   Explain: without it, scheduling a post would be a way around the rule.
3. Rewrite the generated test so it calls `host.invokeHook("content:beforePublish", …)` twice: with a post that has a cover (allowed), and with one that doesn't (cancelled, with our reason). Build both posts in the shape the host sends, `{ id, status, data: { featured_image } }`, so the test fails if the hook reads the wrong path. Don't test generation.
   Explain: generation needs Replicate, so we check it live instead, and the tests stay fast and free.
4. In `../{{pluginDir}}`, run `pnpm run validate`, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run test` and `pnpm run build`.
   Explain: in one line, what `build` writes to `dist/`.

End with a short table of the four commands and their results.

children.text: With the prompt below you are instructing the agent to install and deploy the plugin you created earlier. The instructions tell the agent to check your Workers plan and based on that decide the runtime.

body.label: Copy this prompt into your agent
body.text:
Install the Cover Images plugin in my site, and deploy it. {{explain}}

Steps:

1. In `{{siteDir}}`, run `pnpm add file:../{{pluginDir}}`.
Explain: the site now imports the built plugin like any other package.
Also tell me: whenever we change the plugin after this, bump `version` in `../{{pluginDir}}/package.json`, run `pnpm run build` there, and run `pnpm add file:../{{pluginDir}}` again before deploying. pnpm copies the package instead of linking it, and EmDash caches a sandboxed plugin by ID and version, so with the same version the site keeps running the old code.
2. Ask me which plan this account is on: Workers Free, or Workers Paid (the workshop's enterprise account counts as Paid). Then register the plugin in `astro.config.mjs`:
   - Free: import it and add it to `plugins: []` inside `emdash({ … })`.
   - Paid: uncomment the `LOADER` binding under `worker_loaders` in `wrangler.jsonc`, add `sandboxRunner: sandbox()` (imported from `@emdash-cms/cloudflare`), add the plugin to `sandboxed: []`, and check that `src/worker.ts` exports `PluginBridge`.
Explain, honestly: on Free the plugin runs in-process, so the capability gates on `ctx` still apply, but its code could call `fetch()` directly. On Paid it runs in its own isolate, where it can't.
3. Check that the Worker has `EMDASH_ENCRYPTION_KEY`: `pnpm wrangler secret list`. If it's missing, set it from `.env` without printing it: `grep '^EMDASH_ENCRYPTION_KEY=' .env | cut -d= -f2- | pnpm wrangler secret put EMDASH_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
Explain: without this key, the site refuses to save secret settings.
4. Run `pnpm run typecheck`, commit, and deploy with `pnpm run deploy`.

Then stop. End by telling me to finish the setup in my admin (admin URL on its own line), and that the steps are on the workshop page.

body.prompt:
Delete everything this workshop created on Cloudflare. {{narrate}}

1. Find the real names: the Worker, the D1 database and the R2 bucket from `{{siteDir}}/wrangler.jsonc`. They may differ from the defaults. The first deploy also created a KV namespace for sessions, named after the Worker with `-session` on the end: find its ID with `pnpm wrangler kv namespace list`.
2. List exactly what you'll delete, and wait for my yes.
3. Empty and delete the R2 bucket (`pnpm wrangler r2 bucket delete <name>`; if it isn't empty, tell me to empty it in the dashboard first), then delete the D1 database (`pnpm wrangler d1 delete <name>`), the KV namespace (`pnpm wrangler kv namespace delete --namespace-id <id>`) and the Worker (`pnpm wrangler delete <name>`).
4. Remove the `emdash-site` MCP server from your config.

Don't touch any other Workers, databases, namespaces or buckets. End with a short list of what's gone, and remind me that the local `{{workspaceDir}}` folder is still on my machine, and that my Replicate token keeps working until I revoke it in my Replicate account.
